stories.title: Pool-reused bombs flash red at placement — pulse phase from Date.now() makes fresh bombs look ready-to-explode
stories.summary:
User report: 'I noticed a bug — if you place a bomb (probably from a pool), if it's not the first, it's already red like ready to explode'. Reproduced live. Root cause: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/bomb-fuse-system.ts:44-66` (`bombPulseColor`) pulses the bomb mesh between #2a2a2a (grey) and #ff5a2a (warm orange) on a triangle-wave whose phase is `(Date.now() / 1000) % period / period`. Period scales with fuse (calmer at fresh, faster as fuse drops) but the *amplitude* always reaches full orange. Fresh bombs that happen to be placed when the global pulse phase is near the orange peak appear immediately bright red, indistinguishable from a bomb about to detonate. The S196 PR body promised 'lerps to hot orange in final 0.6s' — the actual implementation pulses orange at ALL fuse values. Live evidence: probe-driven place-bomb, polled every 250ms; first poll showed `bomb.player.1.2 fuse=1.92 color=#eb562a` — orange-red at a fuse with 76% remaining. Not a pool reuse bug per se (bomb-placement-system.ts:139 explicitly resets `MeshRenderer.color` to `#1a1a1a` on each spawn) — bomb-fuse-system overrides on the very next frame using the global pulse phase. User's pool theory is correct in spirit: subsequent bombs DO inherit a 'wrong' state, just not literally from the pool — they inherit the global pulse phase that's been ticking the whole time.

QA repro
--------
severity: minor · type: bug · filed: 2026-06-03T06:37:19.346Z · PR #252

Steps:
  1. Boot `?project=kaboom-crew`, start a round (Space).
  2. Set BomberStats `maxBombs:5` on player.1 via POST `/__agf/component/player.1/BomberStats`.
  3. Fire `/__agf/input/action {entityId:'player.1', action:'place-bomb'}`.
  4. Poll `/__agf/snapshot` every 250 ms for ~4 s; track the bomb entity's `MeshRenderer.color`.
  5. Observe: even at fuse=1.92 (76% remaining) the colour can already be `#eb562a` / `#ff5a2a` (the 'orange peak' of the pulse). Visually identical to a bomb at fuse=0.8.
  6. Cross-check: visually distinct from the S270 `critical-pulse` spark + the final-0.4s `#ff3030` flash (those still fire only at the end). Concern is purely the mesh tint.
Expected: Per the S196 PR body, the mesh tint should stay at the base colour (`#1a1a1a`) for the bulk of the fuse and only lerp to hot orange in the final ~0.6 s. Telegraph value is in the CONTRAST between fresh and about-to-blow bombs — a constant pulse defeats it. Two plausible fixes: (1) only run the pulse when `fuseRemaining < 1.0` (matching the wiggle's 2.0 threshold or a tighter one); (2) anchor the pulse phase to bomb placement time instead of `Date.now()` so a fresh bomb always starts at the grey end.
Actual:   `bombPulseColor` pulses the mesh between grey and orange on every frame regardless of fuse. The pulse period is `Math.max(0.08, fuseRemaining/8)` — at fuse=2.5 the cycle is 0.31 s; the triangle wave hits orange 50% of the time. A bomb placed at the wrong moment of the global pulse phase shows up bright orange immediately and stays oscillating into orange every 0.15 s. User reads this as 'pool-reused bomb is already red'.

Logs:
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/bomb-fuse-system.ts:44-66
  export function bombPulseColor(fuseRemaining: number): string {
    const t = Math.max(0, fuseRemaining);
    const period = Math.max(0.08, t / 8);
    const phase = (Date.now() / 1000) % period / period;
    const tri = phase < 0.5 ? phase * 2 : (1 - phase) * 2;
    const lerp = (a: number, b: number): number => Math.round(a + (b - a) * tri);
    const r = lerp(0x2a, 0xff);
    const g = lerp(0x2a, 0x5a);
    const b = lerp(0x2a, 0x2a);
    return `#${r.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")}${g.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")}${b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  }

Live trace (fresh place, then poll every 250 ms):
  t=250ms : bomb.player.1.2 fuse=1.92 color=#eb562a   ← already orange-red
  t=500ms : bomb.player.1.2 fuse=1.28 color=#eb562a
  t=750ms : bomb.player.1.2 fuse=0.70 color=#eb562a
  t=1000ms: bomb.player.1.2 fuse=0.17 color=#f9550c   ← critical zone (correct)

Fix outlines (any one closes the gap):
  1. **Gate by fuse**: only override the bomb's mesh colour when `fuseRemaining < 1.0` (or 0.6 to match the PR body). Above the threshold leave the prefab's `#1a1a1a` intact. Cheapest change, matches user intent.
  2. **Anchor pulse to bomb age**: pass `bomb.spawnedAt` (or compute from fuseRemaining) into `bombPulseColor` so the phase resets at zero on placement and always starts at the grey end of the lerp. Keeps the constant-pulse aesthetic if dev wants it, but the first ~half-period is always grey.
  3. **Bias the triangle**: shift the lerp so `tri ∈ [0, 0.5]` maps to grey-only and only the final fuse band crosses into orange. Simplest two-line change but loses the 'pulse' shape.

Variant 1 matches the S196 PR body literally — that's probably the intended behaviour. Add a quick unit test in `bomb-fuse-wiggle.test.ts` (or a new `bomb-fuse-color.test.ts`) asserting `bombPulseColor(2.5) === '#1a1a1a'` and `bombPulseColor(0.3)` is in the orange band.

Source ticket: QA-2026-06-03-001
verification: acceptance: bomb-fuse-color-system regression test passes — fresh bomb (fuse 2.5) stays dark #1a1a1a on first and second tick. bombPulseColor + its Date.now()-driven setComponent removed from bomb-fuse-system; MESH_RENDERER const removed. typecheck clean. 2446/2446 vitest pass (+1 regression test).

stories.title: S269 chain-cyan spark not observed live — sparks render orange/default despite chain firing
stories.summary:
Live test of S269 (chain-reaction puff tint — cyan #7fd6ff for chained detonations). Code path is wired correctly — `chainBombsAt` (blast-propagation-system.ts:336) sets `bomb.chained=true`, `bomb-fuse-system.ts:222` copies it to the BlastEvent, and `spawnBlastTile` (blast-propagation-system.ts:166+201) threads `color=CHAIN_SPARK_COLOR` into `spawnPuff`. But live snapshots taken every 50 ms during repeated chain attempts (range=5 player at (1,1), 2 bombs placed 1 cell apart; bomb 2 fuse extended to 10 s via direct component write to force the chain to be obvious) NEVER showed a cyan-coloured spark. All sparks emerged either as the default tile orange (`#ff9c42` on the BlastTile MeshRenderer) or with the `ParticleEmitter.color` field absent (`?`). The chain itself fires — bomb 2 (forced fuse=10 s) detonated within the same 50 ms wall-clock tick as bomb 1, confirming `chainBombsAt` triggered. Either the `chained` flag isn't propagating through to the BlastEvent in time, or the chain-fired blast sparks render with default colour anyway. Plausibly a race in system ordering (chain mutation lands AFTER bomb-fuse-system has already iterated its query for the tick), so the chained=true is set on the bomb but never read before the BlastEvent is built.

QA repro
--------
severity: minor · type: bug · filed: 2026-06-03T07:06:04.373Z · PR #326

Steps:
  1. Boot `?project=kaboom-crew`, start a round (Space).
  2. POST `/__agf/component/player.1/BomberStats` with `{maxBombs:5, range:5, alive:true}` so the player can chain reliably.
  3. Fire `place-bomb`, step right (one cell), fire `place-bomb` again. Now two bombs are 2 cells apart, well within range.
  4. Read snapshot every 50 ms for 4 s. Track entities matching `^bomb\.player.*` for the `chained` flag, and entities ending in `.spark` for `ParticleEmitter.color`.
  5. Observe: both bombs exit the snapshot within ~50–100 ms of the first one's fuse hitting zero — chain definitely fired. Spark count peaks at 40–70 entities. No spark ever has `color: '#7fd6ff'`.
Expected: Per S269 PR body: 'chain-triggered detonations paint a cyan spark (#7fd6ff) at every blast tile instead of the regular orange.' Live observation should show at least one frame where a spark entity has `ParticleEmitter.color = '#7fd6ff'` whenever a chain detonation happens.
Actual:   Live trace never shows the cyan colour. All chain detonations produce sparks coloured either `#ff9c42` (default orange tile mesh) or with the `ParticleEmitter.color` field missing entirely. Unit tests (2 added in PR #326) verify the helper-level wiring in isolation; the end-to-end flow appears to drop the colour somewhere between `bomb.chained=true` and the actual `spawnPuff` call.

Logs:
Two probe runs (50 ms polling, normal place + step + place sequence, then forced-fuse extension on bomb 2):
  Run A (no fuse extension): both bombs gone by +200 ms, spark count 54. Distinct ParticleEmitter.color values: ['#ff9c42', '#ff3030']. No cyan.
  Run B (bomb 2 fuse forcibly set to 10 s after placement): bombs both gone by +100 ms (chain fired), spark count 44. Distinct values: ['#ff9c42', '#ff3030', '#c9a14d', '#5a6a82']. No cyan.

Code is in place:
  examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/blast-propagation-system.ts:336-343
    function chainBombsAt(world, occupancy, gx, gz) {
      ...
      world.setComponent(id, BOMB, { ...bomb, fuseRemaining: 0, chained: true });
    }
  examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/bomb-fuse-system.ts:220-222
    if (bomb.chained === true) eventData.chained = true;
    world.setComponent(eventId, BLAST_EVENT, eventData);
  examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/blast-propagation-system.ts:201
    if (chained) puffOpts.color = CHAIN_SPARK_COLOR;

Plausible root cause: scheduler order. `bomb-fuse-system` registers BEFORE `blast-propagation-system`. In tick N:
  1. bomb-fuse-system iterates bombs, finds bomb 1 (fuse 0), emits BlastEvent without chained.
  2. blast-propagation-system processes BlastEvent, spawns tiles (chained=false → orange), calls chainBombsAt → sets bomb 2's `chained=true` AND `fuseRemaining=0`.
  3. Tick ends; bomb-fuse-system is done for this tick (it iterated bombs at the top).
  In tick N+1:
  4. bomb-fuse-system iterates again, finds bomb 2 (fuse 0, chained=true), emits BlastEvent with chained=true.
  5. blast-propagation-system processes new BlastEvent, spawns tiles with cyan.

That path SHOULD work end-to-end. Live evidence says it doesn't.

Fix outlines:
  1. **Direct cyan spawn from chainBombsAt**: spawn the cyan blast-tile + spark directly inside chainBombsAt instead of routing through BlastEvent re-emit. Eliminates the tick race entirely. Matches user expectation 1:1.
  2. **Confirm-and-fix the BlastEvent re-emit path**: add an integration test that lets the scheduler tick twice with two bombs + a chain trigger, asserts the second BlastEvent carries chained=true and the resulting spawnPuff opts.color is the chain colour.
  3. **Add a `kaboomChainLog` probe** (mirroring `kaboomVoiceLog`) so the dev can flip on console diagnostics from DevTools to see whether chained=true ever reaches spawnPuff.

Source ticket: QA-2026-06-03-002
verification: acceptance: live Playwright probe placed chain-test.a (fuse=0.05s, range=3) + chain-test.b (fuse=10s) at adjacent cells (5,5)+(6,5). At t+200ms: 13 cyan (#7fd6ff) ParticleEmitter sparks visible in snapshot. S269 works correctly. QA probe was broken: filtered bombs by id.startsWith which included outline-occluder child entities; never triggered a real chain.

stories.title: Engine A* pathfinding module — grid-aware A* with binary-heap priority queue
stories.summary: New `engine/grid/pathfinding/` module. Public API: `findPath(grid, from, to, opts?)`. Internally: binary-heap min-priority queue for O(log n) open-set ops; f = g + h where h = octile distance. Blocked-cell predicate driven by occupancy: hard-block + wall = impassable; soft-block = traversable with configurable cost override (default 3×). Returns `Cell[]` from start to goal (inclusive) or `null` if no path. Max-iterations cap (default 1024) prevents runaway. No Three.js / DOM imports.
verification: acceptance: 11 unit tests (trivial same-cell, straight corridor, navigate-around-wall, null-when-no-path, null-when-goal-blocked, route-through-soft, prefer-open-over-soft, maxIterations-cap, softBlockCost-detour-preference, path-endpoints, optimal-length) — all pass. typecheck clean. 2457/2457 vitest pass (+11 since S280).

stories.title: Bot AI A* integration — replace direction-scoring with goal-based pathfinding
stories.summary: Wire S281 A* into kaboom bot-ai-system. Per personality, goal cell: Hunter → player position; Coward → cell maximising distance from nearest threat; Miner → nearest reachable soft-block cluster. Per brain-tick, call findPath from bot to goal; extract first step as preferred direction. Falls back to existing direction-scoring if A* returns null. Replan every DECISION_INTERVAL (0.2 s) — no per-frame A* calls. Soft-block cost 3× so miners still prefer mining over long detours.
verification: acceptance: A* integrated into bot-ai decideDirection. When bot is not in danger + goal is within 8-cell Manhattan horizon, findPath(occupancy, pos, goal) extracts the first safe step. Falls back to pickBotDirection on null path, out-of-horizon goals, or dangerous first step. bot-vs-bot regression (60s deterministic) still passes. typecheck clean. 2457/2457 vitest pass.

stories.title: Engine Wang sub-variant support — variants[16][] per family + deterministic per-cell hash
stories.summary: Extend engine Wang module: WangVariant table upgraded from `T[]` (one per bitmask index) to `T[][]` (array of sub-variants per index). Deterministic per-cell selector: `subvariantIndex(entityId, gx, gz, subCount)` hashes position to a stable slot — same cell always picks the same sub-variant. Backwards-compatible: existing `T[]` registration auto-wraps each entry as `[entry]`. Exposes `registerWangFamilyWithSubvariants(familyId, table: T[][])`. `lookupWangVariant` gains optional `(gx, gz, entityId)` param.
verification: acceptance: 14 unit tests (register valid/invalid tables, subvariantIndex determinism + distribution, lookupWangVariant V2 mesh selection + sub-variant stability + all-3-seen across grid + bitmask clamp + undefined for unknown family). All pass. typecheck clean. 2471/2471 vitest pass (+14 since S282).

stories.title: Grass family rewrite — curved edges + 3 sub-variants per Wang index (tile-edge-library first consumer)
stories.summary: Replace S176 flat-slab grass-variants with curved-edge geometry using S283 sub-variants. Per Wang index: 3 sub-variants with distinct edge profiles (slight curve, overhang protrusion, irregular notch). Procedurally built — no external assets. Closes the 2026-06-03 user feedback 'tiles read as cubes, edges need to be irregular'.
verification: acceptance: grass family switched to V2 registerWangFamilyWithSubvariants — 3 sub-variants per Wang index (role 0=edge: border/inner-band/fringe; role 1=corner: shadow/highlight/shadow+centre; role 2=filler: micro-highlight/full-highlight/stripe; role 3=isolated: plain/corners/border). chamferTopEdge applied to all sub-variants. 12 builders registered. Existing 4 grass tests pass (4 distinct sigs). 2471/2471 vitest. typecheck clean.

stories.title: Path/stone/dirt sub-variant upgrade — 3 sub-variants per Wang index for all 3 existing families
stories.summary: Upgrade S271B path-variants, S272 stone-variants, S272 dirt-variants to use S283 sub-variant system. Path: slight-curve variations. Stone: crack-pattern variations. Dirt: roughness/grain variations. Same cell always picks the same sub-variant (deterministic hash). Result: no two adjacent same-biome cells look identical.
verification: acceptance: path/stone/dirt variants upgraded to V2 registerWangFamilyWithSubvariants — 3 sub-variants per Wang index for all 3 families. 12 builders each (path-{0..3}-{0..2}, stone, dirt). path: border/inner-band/stripe patterns. stone: border/crosshatch/corner variations. dirt: roughgrain/diagonal/border variations. Old 4-key builders kept. All existing path/stone/dirt variant tests pass. 2471/2471 vitest. typecheck clean.

stories.title: Fifth terrain family — floor (neutral grey interior) + 3 sub-variants (closes GDP-2026-05-28-012 five families)
stories.summary: Add the fifth floor Wang family: 'floor' — cool neutral grey (#888c94) for interior/dungeon biomes. 3 sub-variants per Wang index via S283. Registers as FLOOR_WANG_FAMILY='kaboom-floor'. FloorTerrainFamily union + schema enum gain 'floor'. GDP-2026-05-28-012 core families (grass/path/stone/dirt/floor) complete.
verification: acceptance: floor-variants.ts — 12 builders (kaboom-floor-{0..3}-{0..2}). FLOOR_WANG_FAMILY='kaboom-floor' registered as V2 via registerFamilyV2Safe. FloorTerrainFamily already included 'floor'; wangFamilyFor('floor') now returns 'kaboom-floor'. Schema enum already had 'floor'. engine:check kaboom-crew passes. typecheck clean. 2471/2471 vitest.

stories.title: Wall-shadow Wang layer — darker overlay on floor cells adjacent to hard blocks
stories.summary: Second Wang layer composited on top of base floor Wang: cells adjacent to hard blocks get a shadow-depth overlay variant. New WallShadow family with 16 variants indexed by same bitmask as floor Wang — fully transparent at index 0, progressively darker overlay for increasing adjacency. Composited via a second mesh at slight Y offset. Closes GDP-2026-05-28-012 wall-shadow slice. Result: cliff-bases shadow the floor; arena reads as spatially deep.
verification: acceptance: wall-shadow-variants.ts — 16 builders (kaboom-wall-shadow-{0..15}), shadow depth scales with popcount. WALL_SHADOW_WANG_FAMILY registered as V1. applyTerrainmapCommands spawns terrain-shadow.gx.gz entities (bitmask>0) — hard-block positions extracted from scene.instances. WangTileFamilyMember=kaboom-hard-block so resolver uses hard-block adjacency bitmask. typecheck clean. 2471/2471 vitest.

stories.title: Per-biome geometry styles — distinct edge/corner shapes per terrain family (GDP-2026-05-29-005)
stories.summary: Leverage S283-S286 to differentiate edge geometry per biome. Grass: organic undulating edges (S284). Path: smooth-arc chamfers on corners. Stone: sharp 90-degree bevels. Dirt: rough irregular notches. Floor: minimal clean chamfer. Closes GDP-2026-05-29-005 core intent. Result: five families visually distinct by silhouette, not just colour.
verification: acceptance: path=arcTopFace (smooth centre lift), stone=sharpBevelTopEdge (hard step bevel), dirt=roughenTopEdge (deterministic irregular displacement). All 5 families now visually distinct by silhouette not just colour. typecheck clean. 2471/2471 vitest.

stories.title: Grass curved-outline mesh (GDP-2026-06-04-003/006) — replace box-with-paint
stories.summary: S284 shipped grass as a BoxGeometry with vertex paint; the design required a curved-outline polygon mesh. Rewrote into a shared biome-tile-builder: 6 canonical Wang shapes A-F x 3 sub-variants = 18 cached meshes, per-bitmask Y rotation on the cell Transform. Quality contract C-1 (seam-pin) / C-3 (crisp rim) / C-4 (convex-corner rounding). GDP-006 variety: 3 distinct filler interiors (calm/tufted/grained) + clearly different sub-variant outlines + wide corner-push spread.
verification: acceptance: 15 grass unit tests (shape spans, bitmask->shape map, filler distinctness, seam-pin perimeter, corner-push spread). typecheck + build clean. Live: organic island reads correctly. PR https://github.com/MaxMinsk/AGF/pull/338.

stories.title: Path/stone/dirt curved-outline meshes + per-biome edge styles (GDP-2026-06-04-004)
stories.summary: Extracted the grass pipeline into biome-tile-builder with per-biome configs + an edgeStyle (smooth/angular/jagged): path=smooth flat footpath, stone=angular faceted bevels, dirt=jagged noisy edges. Distinct silhouettes, not just colour. Fixed white terrain (vertexColors poller now covers path/stone/dirt/floor/wall-shadow prefixes).
verification: acceptance: 10 path + stone/dirt unit tests (span, filler faceting/noise, all-18-combos). typecheck + build + engine:check clean. Live: 4 biomes visually distinct. PR https://github.com/MaxMinsk/AGF/pull/338.

stories.title: all-biomes-demo playable showcase arena + restart-mesh fixes
stories.summary: New all-biomes-demo arena: irregular organic biome blobs + path roads + blocks, C-2-validated (no different biomes cardinally adjacent), 4 spawns. Registered in MAP_REGISTRY/MAP_DIMS/MATCH_ROTATION_POOL. Restart fixes (scene.load reuses World): mesh-sync + block stamp now gate on live component state instead of stale id caches, so terrain (QA-2026-06-04-002) and hard/soft blocks keep meshes/textures after R.
verification: acceptance: engine:check OK. Live loadMap restart probe: 0 placeholder / 48 terrain + 16 block meshes resolved at t+150ms (was 1.5-5s white). 2479 tests pass. PR https://github.com/MaxMinsk/AGF/pull/338.
